title: Ridge, Lasso & Elastic Net
interviewAnswer: Ridge uses L2 regularization to shrink coefficients; Lasso uses L1 and can set coefficients exactly to zero; Elastic Net combines both, often helping with correlated features.
why: Ridge, Lasso & Elastic Net appears frequently in data-science work because it connects mathematical assumptions to practical decisions, diagnostics and failure modes.
deepDive: Ridge uses L2 regularization to shrink coefficients; Lasso uses L1 and can set coefficients exactly to zero; Elastic Net combines both, often helping with correlated features. Scale features before coefficient-penalty comparisons. Tune strength with validation. A strong practitioner separates the modeling assumption from the estimation procedure, checks diagnostics rather than trusting a single score, and explains what would make the method inappropriate.
workedExample: For thousands of correlated marketing features, Elastic Net can stabilize estimates while selecting a sparse-ish subset.
commonMistakes: Applying the method without checking its assumptions or data-generating process.
Choosing it because it is familiar rather than comparing against an appropriate baseline.
followUps: What assumptions does Ridge, Lasso & Elastic Net make?
How would you validate or debug Ridge, Lasso & Elastic Net in practice?
production: In production, validate assumptions on real data, monitor the quantities that can drift, and keep a simple baseline so added complexity has a measurable reason to exist.

lab.goal: See how L1/L2 regularization changes coefficients.
lab.buildIt:
import numpy as np
from sklearn.datasets import make_regression
X,y=make_regression(n_samples=250,n_features=12,n_informative=4,noise=15,random_state=0)
lab.useIt:
from sklearn.pipeline import make_pipeline
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
from sklearn.linear_model import Ridge,Lasso
ridge=make_pipeline(StandardScaler(),Ridge(alpha=10)).fit(X,y)
lasso=make_pipeline(StandardScaler(),Lasso(alpha=3,max_iter=10000)).fit(X,y)
print(ridge[-1].coef_)
print(lasso[-1].coef_)
lab.shipIt: Tune alpha with leakage-safe cross-validation; persist the full preprocessing+model pipeline so training and serving use identical scaling.
